title: Injective edge of the resolution Hom double complex is a quasi-isomorphism
statement: Let $R$ be a commutative ring and $X,M$ be $R$-modules. Let $P_\bullet\to X$ be a nonnegative projective resolution (each $P_i$ projective and the augmented chain complex exact), and let $M\to E^\bullet$ be an injective resolution [def-sp-injective-resolutions]. Form the first-quadrant double complex $K^{i,j}=\operatorname{Hom}_R(P_i,E^j)$, with horizontal differential precomposition by $d_P$ and vertical differential postcomposition by $d_E$, and total complex [def-sp-double-complex-total] with differential $d_h+(-1)^i d_v$. The canonical cochain map $\operatorname{Hom}_R(X,E^\bullet)\to\operatorname{Tot}(K)$ whose component in degree $n$ is precomposition by $P_0\to X$ followed by inclusion of the $(0,n)$ summand is a quasi-isomorphism, meaning it induces an isomorphism on every cohomology module.

source.place: Tag 0954, proof of Lemma 47.8.2, Ext computed by an injective resolution; explicit double-complex comparison

proof.text: Use the concrete total Hom complex and horizontal edge constructed in the projective-edge module. Define a:Hom(X,E)→K.X 0 using precomposition with P_0→X. Its composite with the next horizontal differential is zero by d_P followed by the augmentation being zero. Its total augmentation is exactly the injective edge.

For each injective E^n, linear Yoneda preserves limits and epimorphisms: these facts hold for its composite with the forgetful functor by representability and injectivity and reflect back to modules. It therefore preserves homology. Oppose P→X[0], which remains a quasi-isomorphism, then apply this exact functor. Identify the source with Hom(X,E^n)[0] by the identity at zero and the isomorphisms between zero objects in positive degrees. Equality with the required column augmentation follows from from_single_hom_ext and equality of the degree-zero component. This is proved from Mathlib in Lean.

Apply the cited first-quadrant column augmentation criterion to K, a, the explicitly constructed injective edge and these column quasi-isomorphisms. This gives the desired edge quasi-isomorphism in all degrees, including zero.
